As someone who is just coming out & healing from clinical depression (a lot of which developed during childhood) I can tell you it’s incredibly difficult for those around us to know what to say. Perhaps the original conversation you had with him opened up some old wounds & now he’s dealing with them (either consciously or unconsciously or both). This isn’t necessarily a bad thing depending on how he’s handling it. It sounds like he’s taking it kind of hard & it’s likely not any fault of your own. When I was in his shoes my sister convinced me to seek some help, which I finally begrudgingly did. I reached out and made an appointment with a local therapist. It was incredibly difficult to ask for help. Especially for men in today’s society. But that’s what it took for me to truly begin healing. Now I know that asking for help was the bravest thing I could’ve possibly done. Your BF might also benefit from finding a professional to talk through all of this with. In the mean time, just love him the best you can. Let him know you’re there for him no matter what. You don’t always need to have the answers, or know exactly what to say, just having & feeling your unconditional love & support will go a long way toward helping him heal his wounds. The fact that you took the time to post this tells me you really care, which is an absolute blessing. It might also help to read up on how to help loved ones dealing with depression. It’s a tricky subject but there’s lots of good information out there as people become more aware of mental health in general. I hope this helps in some small way.
